SUBMISSION NOTE - parsimagma refuter

Compressed data or binary blobs: none. The solver is plain Python with no
embedded payload; the construction corpus is regenerated by a loop at runtime.

Sources drawn on: no Contributor Network item. The ordering in PRIORITY comes
from my own prior open-source work, https://github.com/carlok/parsimagma
(Apache-2.0), described under "Reproducing the ordering" below. Nothing else.


WHAT IT DOES

One strategy, applied to every problem: enumerate small linear and affine
magmas  x o y = a*x + b*y + c  over Z/m, keep the first that satisfies the
hypothesis and violates the goal, and certify it with plain `decide`.

A second tier handles the problems the first cannot reach structurally. On
those, thousands of linear magmas satisfy the hypothesis and every one
satisfies the goal too - 7,298 of them on one sampled problem. The fix is the
construction in the Equational Theories Project blueprint's "Magma cohomology"
chapter: an extension of a base magma B by Z/p,

    (x, s) o (y, t) = (x o y, alpha*s + beta*t + c(x, y))

where base and fibre may both satisfy both laws and the cocycle c breaks the
goal. Once B, p, alpha and beta are fixed, satisfying a law is a linear
condition on c, so the working cocycles form a subspace found by elimination
rather than by enumerating p^(|B|^2).

No LLM calls.


WHY A LINEAR SWEEP IS THE RIGHT FIRST MOVE

Measured over the ETP's own implication graph, on the 13,855,357 implications
it records as false:

    instances   false implications refuted   share
    4 (all of Z/2)          11,871,871       85.7%
    25                      13,472,458       97.2%
    2,786 (full corpus)     13,834,667       99.85%

PRIORITY is the prefix of a greedy set cover computed against that graph, which
is why Z/2 comes first and most problems finish in milliseconds. On 400
uniformly sampled false order-4 implications the two tiers refute 393 (98.2%),
and 342 of the tier-1 hits are settled by a two-element magma.

The tail is generated, not stored: x o y = 7x + 7y over Z/13 alone refutes 268
of the 1062 implications Vampire left undecided in Janota, arXiv:2508.15856 -
instances that Vampire fmb, Mace4 and z3 on a ground encoding all fail to find.


MEASURED ON THE STRESS TEST

Against the 200-problem stage2_stress_test set, which mirrors the graded
distribution:

    category               false     true
    order4_normal          23/25     0/25
    order4_hard            17/25     0/25
    order4_extra_hard       0/25     0/25
    order5_normal          15/25     0/25
    total                  55/100    0/100

55/200. Two things that makes plain. The extra_hard category is selected
against exactly this method and the corpus reaches none of it, so the 98.2%
above - which is over uniformly sampled false implications from the ETP graph -
does not transfer to a curated set. And the solver takes a zero on all 100 true
implications by design.


SCOPE, STATED PLAINLY

This solver refutes; it does not prove. It answers nothing on true implications
and takes the zero, which the scoring rules make costless.


REPRODUCING THE ORDERING

The corpus, the coverage figures and the greedy cover are in
https://github.com/carlok/parsimagma (Apache-2.0), which computes signatures
for ~2,786 constructions over the 4694-law set and reports coverage against the
ETP graph. PRIORITY in the solver is the first twenty rows of the greedy cover
over false implications. Everything else is a plain loop over (m, a, b, c), so
no part of the solver needs the repository to run.


IMPLEMENTATION NOTES

- The tier-1 operation is emitted as a Lean function, not through finOpTable.
  That helper reads its argument one character at a time, so a table entry of
  ten or more is silently split in two and every carrier above 9 is wrong.
  Tier-2 certificates do use finOpTable, capped at carrier 10 where it is safe.
- Candidates are skipped when carrier^arity exceeds a cap, since the problem
  set contains six-variable laws where a naive sweep does not terminate.
- Certificates depend on propext alone; native_decide is not used anywhere.
